question: Should the canonical `agent-transcript` skill begin automatically discovering and rendering GitHub Copilot local sessions after final-head privacy proof is supplied?
rationale: This changes which private local data the skill may read and later place in public GitHub bodies; tests and contributor-authored evidence cannot determine the repository’s acceptable disclosure boundary.

options.title: Approve the bounded Copilot source
options.body: Approve the new source only after a redacted final-head run demonstrates the allowlist, tool-output omission, and path/URL secret redaction.

options.title: Require opt-in discovery
options.body: Keep Copilot parsing available but require an explicit source or flag so existing workflows never scan Copilot sessions automatically.

options.title: Defer the source addition
options.body: Keep the current agent sources and revisit Copilot support after maintainers define a broader transcript-data policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded Copilot source
recommendation.body: Approve the new source only after a redacted final-head run demonstrates the allowlist, tool-output omission, and path/URL secret redaction.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the canonical skill’s persisted privacy contract rather than the proposed branch alone.
